text:
alex: Quick sync — proposing a focused benchmark plan for KV prefix caching that isolates kernel selection and batching heuristics. want to make sure it's apples-to-apples and catches concurrency correctness.
priya: SG. high-level goals? p95/p99 latency, token cost delta, hit-rate curve vs memory, and correctness under concurrent writes/evicts?
alex: exactly. also capture warmup/backfill behavior (cold start to steady hit-rate), eviction churn under mixed seq lengths, and impact of batching heuristics on effective throughput.
jordan: +1. i'd add deterministic replay traces so we can compare different kernel selections with identical request ordering.
sam: proposal: run three workloads: 1) synthetic iid seq lengths (short/med/long), 2) production replay (sanitized traces, same concurrency shape), 3) mixed bursty traffic (ramp + spikes). keep model binary and kernel fixed per trial.
alex: plan details in short:
- baseline: current kernel selector (v3) + batching heuristics (dyn-batch-v2) + kv cache size 1.5GB
- variants: kernel selector forced to kernel-a / kernel-b, batching set to static vs dyn, kv size sweep [256MB, 512MB, 1GB, 1.5GB, 3GB]
- metrics: hit_rate, cold_to_steady_time (s), p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cpu/gpu utilization, evictions/sec, correctness errors (mismatched prefix responses)

priya: how will we measure "correctness errors"? we need deterministic checksums for outputs of cached vs uncached runs.
alex: yes — for each request we store a short response fingerprint (sha1 of normalized tokens). run cached-enabled and cache-bypassed with identical input stream and diff fingerprints. failures flagged if mismatch > 0.
jordan: good. also log per-key version ids so we can spot stale reads during eviction races.
sam: concurrency repro: i built a small harness where N clients issue overlapping prefix writes (backfill) while readers request the same prefixes. saw rare stale reads at high N (>=128) in earlier runs.
perf-bot: benchmark job queued: bench-kv-prefix/1789345678/run-1 (synthetic-iid)

ci-bot: note: ensure we pin commit abc1234 for runtime and model v2.1 to keep comparisons fair.

priya: good call. also freeze quantization profile and disable speculative kernels so kernel selector only picks among validated set.
alex: commands to run replay harness: 
```
./tools/replay-harness --trace traces/prod_sanitized.json --concurrency 64 --rate 500 --pin-kernel kernel-a --kv-max-bytes 1073741824 --batching dyn
```
and for synthetic: 
```
./tools/synth-load --pattern iid --seq-dist "short:0.7,med:0.25,long:0.05" --qps 800 --duration 1200
```
jordan: when comparing kernels, make sure to collect perf counters: active_warp_stalls, mem_bandwidth, l2_hit_ratio — these explain p99 diffs.
sam: found a micro-regression earlier: switching batching heuristic to dyn-v3 decreased p99 by 8% normally, but under high backfill it increased evictions/sec by 3x — likely due to different early-batch sizing causing more duplicate prefix writes.
priya: can you paste the profile snippet that pointed to the issue?
sam: paste: 
```
# perf summary (dyn-v2 vs dyn-v3)
p99 latency: 48ms -> 52ms
evictions/sec: 12 -> 38
kv_write_latency_p95: 6ms -> 18ms
hotspot: kv_backfill_worker::apply_prefix (contention on epoch_lock)
```
alex: that epoch_lock contention looks real. possible fixes: sharded locks by prefix-hash, or versioned compare-and-swap so readers never block writers.
jordan: versioned CAS would reduce blocking but increases memory for tombstones. sharded locks might be simpler to test quickly.
priya: for apples-to-apples, we must: pin model, pin runtime commit, use same trace ordering, same QPS, and seed RNG for synthetic workloads. also log seed in output metadata.
alex: agreed. we'll also run each config 3x and report median. use the following naming scheme for artifacts: bench/{trace}/{kernel}/{batching}/{kv_size}/{seed}.tar.gz

sam: reproducible race repro steps I used: 
1) start harness with --concurrency 256 --backfill-rate 2000/s
2) run for 300s
3) grep for "stale-read" in harness output (fingerprint mismatch)
Example log snippet:
```
[2026-01-15T12:04:03Z] reader-173: req id=abcd1234 prefix=usr:42 fingerprint=f1 -> f2 (STALE_READ)
```
perf-bot: regression alert: bench-kv-prefix/run-12 shows p99 +12% vs baseline kernel-a (investigate kernel selection path)

priya: good catch. could kernel-b be doing different attention kernel that increases KV load per token? need to correlate tokenization seq length distribution with kernel choice.
alex: next steps:
- sam: run sharded-lock patch on a small kv size and reproduce with high concurrency (256)
- jordan: collect perf counters and nvprof traces for the p99-regression kernels
- priya: prepare artifact naming and run 3 repeats for each config; upload to s3

sam: will run a quick A/B: kernel-a + dyn-v2 (baseline) vs kernel-a + dyn-v3 (batch change) vs kernel-b + dyn-v2. start with kv=512MB, seed=42, concurrency=[64,128,256]

alex: timeline: try to get initial runs within 24h, aim to have an internal doc with graphs (hit-rate vs time, p99 vs kv size, evictions/sec) and a small appendix with repro steps.
jordan: also add a tiny test in CI that runs a short deterministic prefix concurrency check (N=32) to prevent regressions from landing silently.
priya: i'll draft the CI test and the artifact schema tonight.
alex: thanks all. update thread with links to s3 uploads and perf traces when ready. :rocket:

ci-bot: bench artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/bench/1789345678/ (contains run metadata and profiles)

sam: uploaded initial run logs to s3://redwood-ci/bench/1789345678/run-quick/ — highlights: dyn-v3 shows higher eviction churn at concurrency>=128.

alex: perfect. we'll triage tomorrow in infra sync. closing for now.
